architectural_units.name: User
architectural_units.description: The end user of the portal and applications.

architectural_units.name: Leader Service
architectural_units.description: Microservice responsible for routing communications to the appropriate microservice and managing traffic.

architectural_units.name: Portal Service
architectural_units.description: Microservice providing a centralized interface for accessing applications and hosting frontend binaries.

architectural_units.name: Access Control Service
architectural_units.description: Microservice responsible for user authentication and permission management.

architectural_units.name: Communication Log Service
architectural_units.description: Microservice for logging system communications and providing audit/statistical data.

architectural_units.name: Scheduler Service
architectural_units.description: Microservice for planning and executing automated system tasks.

architectural_units.name: Amazon Web Services
architectural_units.description: Cloud provider hosting the system infrastructure.

architectural_units.name: Amazon RDS
architectural_units.description: Database engine used for data persistence.

architectural_units.name: Angular
architectural_units.description: Frontend framework used for building the SPA.

architectural_units.name: Spring Boot
architectural_units.description: Backend framework used for developing microservices and REST APIs.

architectural_units.name: View
architectural_units.description: Frontend component responsible for UI presentation (HTML/SCSS).

architectural_units.name: ViewModel
architectural_units.description: Frontend component responsible for logic, data processing, and service orchestration (TS).

architectural_units.name: Model
architectural_units.description: Frontend component defining data contracts.

architectural_units.name: Presentation Layer (Controller)
architectural_units.description: Backend layer handling REST requests and responses.

architectural_units.name: Business Logic Layer (Service)
architectural_units.description: Backend layer implementing business rules.

architectural_units.name: Domain Layer (Model)
architectural_units.description: Backend layer defining internal data entities.

architectural_units.name: Contract Layer (DTO/Mapper)
architectural_units.description: Backend layer separating internal models from external API representations.

architectural_units.name: Data Access Layer (Repository)
architectural_units.description: Backend layer interacting with the database.
The User communicates with the Portal Service via the internet.
The Leader Service routes communications to the Scheduler Service.
The Leader Service routes communications to the Access Control Service.
The Leader Service routes communications to the Communication Log Service.
The Leader Service routes communications to the Portal Service.
The Scheduler Service reads from and writes to Amazon RDS.
The Access Control Service reads from and writes to Amazon RDS.
The Communication Log Service reads from and writes to Amazon RDS.
The Portal Service reads from and writes to Amazon RDS.
The View component captures user interactions and sends them to the ViewModel.
The ViewModel orchestrates HTTP calls to the backend Presentation Layer.
The Presentation Layer communicates with the Business Logic Layer.
The Business Logic Layer interacts with the Data Access Layer.
The Data Access Layer interacts with Amazon RDS.

patterns.name: Microservices
patterns.description: The system is divided into small, independent, and autonomous services where each microservice is responsible for a specific functionality and communicates with others via messaging systems.

patterns.name: Cloud Architecture
patterns.description: The application is designed, deployed, and executed using cloud computing services (AWS) instead of local or physical servers, allowing for scalability, availability, and accessibility.

patterns.name: Client-Server
patterns.description: The application organizes code into two distinct components: the client, which formulates service requests, and the server, which receives, processes, and returns responses.

patterns.name: MVVM (Model-View-ViewModel)
patterns.description: Used in the Angular frontend, this pattern separates the user interface (View) from the logic and data processing (ViewModel) and the data contract (Model).

patterns.name: Layered Architecture
patterns.description: The server (backend) organizes code into layers to separate responsibilities: presentation, business logic, data access, domain, and contract layers.

patterns.name: Single-Page Application (SPA)
patterns.description: The client is developed as a Single-Page Application that renders dynamic views and manages internal navigation without reloading the page.
